deep_dive_html:
The Perils of CAM Creep in Tech Leases

For tech startups, the true cost of a lease is rarely found in the base rent; it is buried in the Common Area Maintenance (CAM) provisions. While a fixed rent provides predictability, an ill-defined CAM clause introduces extreme volatility into your monthly burn rate. Landlords frequently exploit vague language to pass through significant, unbudgeted costs that can jeopardize your venture-backed runway.

The Capital Improvement Trap

The most predatory tactic involves the reclassification of capital expenditures as routine maintenance. A sophisticated landlord will attempt to include the full cost of structural replacements—such as a new HVAC system, roof replacement, or parking lot resurfacing—within the annual operating expense pool. Without specific protections, you are essentially subsidizing the landlord's long-term asset appreciation with your operational capital.

  • Uncapped Administrative Fees: Landlords often insert arbitrary percentages for management fees that allow them to extract additional profit under the guise of overhead.
  • Lack of Audit Rights: Without a clause explicitly granting you the right to inspect the landlord's books, you are forced to accept their expense statements at face value.
  • Undefined Operating Expenses: Broad definitions that allow for the inclusion of all costs related to the building can lead to the inclusion of non-controllable items like property taxes or insurance spikes.
  • Absence of Expense Caps: A lack of a controllable expense cap means your year-over-year costs can escalate indefinitely.

Implementing Market-Standard Protections

To neutralize these risks, your lease must include a Controllable Expense Cap, typically limiting the annual increase of non-tax and non-insurance items to a fixed percentage, such as 5%. Furthermore, you must insist that any capital improvements be amortized over their useful life, with only the annual portion of that amortization charged to your CAM share. This ensures that a massive structural repair is spread over many years rather than hitting your P&L in a single quarter.

title: Red Flags in Common Area Maintenance Clauses for Tech Startups
